title: Modus ponens
note: →L splits the goal: one premise proves a, the other uses b.

title: Conjunction commutes
note: ∧R first or ∧L first: both orders reach the axioms.

title: Chained implications
sequent: a -> b, b -> c |- a -> c
note: →R moves a left of ⊢; each →L then uses one hypothesis.

title: Currying
note: Two →R steps before the hypothesis can be used.

title: Distribution
note: ∨L splits into two cases; in LJ each case must choose its disjunct with ∨R.

title: Contraposition
note: A negation is an implication into ⊥, so minimal logic proves this without ex falso.

title: Double negation, introduced
note: Adding ¬¬ is valid in every logic here.

title: De Morgan, the constructive half
note: Holds even in minimal logic; compare its dual, which needs classical logic.

title: Ex falso
note: Minimal logic has no rule for ⊥ left of ⊢; switch to intuitionistic logic and ⊥L closes it.

title: Excluded middle, in LJ
note: LJ keeps one formula right of ⊢, so ∨R must choose a disjunct, and neither is provable.

title: Excluded middle, in LK
note: LK keeps both disjuncts right of ⊢, and ¬R moves a to the left for the axiom.

title: Excluded middle, doubly negated
note: Its double negation is valid in LJ: the hypothesis ¬(a ∨ ¬a) is used twice.

title: Double negation, eliminated
note: Valid in LK; switch to intuitionistic logic to see it fail.

title: Peirce's law
note: Classical without a negation: the proof keeps a twice right of ⊢.

title: De Morgan, the classical half
note: The dual of the constructive half needs LK's two formulas right of ⊢.
